title: Diabetes, hypertension and CKD together
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the patient's diabetes, kidney disease and any related hypertension and dialysis status.
note:
Chief Complaint
Follow-up for chronic kidney disease and type 2 diabetes.

HPI
The patient is an 89-year-old woman presenting for a scheduled follow-up. She reports feeling well overall but notes occasional fatigue. She continues to manage her type 2 diabetes primarily through dietary modifications and has not reported any recent acute symptoms related to her renal function. She remains stable on her current regimen.

Medication List
Multivitamins, Vitamin D supplement.

Exam
The patient appears well-nourished and in no acute distress. She is alert and oriented. Skin is intact without new lesions. Blood pressure is 128/78 mmHg. Heart rate is 72 beats per minute. Lungs are clear to auscultation.

Assessment
1. Chronic kidney disease, stage 4. Recent laboratory results show an eGFR of 22 mL/min/1.73m2.
2. Type 2 diabetes. Currently managed with diet only.

Plan
We will continue to monitor her renal function closely. The patient will maintain her current diet to manage her glucose levels. We will repeat her labs in three months to track her CKD progression.

Electronically signed
P. O'Brien, MD
May 14, 2026
explanations: Type 2 diabetes and CKD are linked by the 'with' convention unless the provider says otherwise: E11.22 (HCC 37).
The CKD stage is coded in addition: N18.4.

distractors.why: The 'with' convention presumes the diabetes caused the CKD.
E11.22 says to use an additional code for the CKD stage.
